name: How do I know if my commercial improvement is too small for a general contractor?

mainEntity.name: When can a property owner use a smaller crew instead of a full commercial builder?
mainEntity.text: When can a property owner use a smaller crew instead of a full commercial builder?

acceptedAnswer.text: Project size alone does not determine whether you need a commercial general contractor. A small project can still be complex if it touches electrical, plumbing, HVAC, accessibility, or fire-safety systems. A full commercial builder is usually the better fit when the work requires coordination across multiple trades, permits, inspections, or occupied-space protection. Smaller cosmetic jobs may be manageable with a lighter construction team if no regulated systems are involved. Owners should think about risk, not just square footage. If a mistake would affect occupancy, opening date, or permit approval, the safer choice is usually a contractor experienced with commercial processes.
acceptedAnswer.description: A project may be too small for a full commercial general contractor if it is limited to very minor cosmetic work with no permit issues, no trade coordination, and no occupied-space risk. Once the job involves multiple trades, inspections, or code-sensitive systems, a commercial contractor is usually the safer choice. The deciding factor is complexity, not just size.
